options: Worse at night or early morning
Worse after meals or on lying down
Only during/after an URTI that is settling
Low-grade evening fever with night sweats
Appetite loss without weight change yet
Episodic wheeze with triggers (dust, cold, exercise)
Breathless lying flat with ankle swelling

red_flags: Cough > 3 weeks with fever, night sweats, or weight loss (TB until excluded)
Cough with SpO2 < 92%, respiratory rate > 30, or confusion
Smoker > 40 years with new persistent cough or voice change
Cough with unilateral chest pain and breathlessness of sudden onset
Stridor or suspected inhaled foreign body
exam: Record temperature, respiratory rate, SpO2, and pulse together
Inspect for cachexia, pallor, and finger clubbing (clubbing → malignancy or chronic suppuration, not simple bronchitis)
Palpate cervical and supraclavicular lymph nodes — hard fixed nodes raise malignancy, matted nodes raise TB
Auscultate all lung zones: focal crackles or bronchial breathing (pneumonia), diffuse wheeze (asthma/COPD), fixed monophonic wheeze (obstructing lesion), basal crackles (heart failure)
Percuss comparing sides for focal dullness (consolidation, effusion)
Examine the nose and posterior pharynx for turbinate swelling and mucus streaming (postnasal drip)
Listen to the voice for hoarseness (recurrent laryngeal involvement by tumour)
Estimate JVP and check ankle oedema (cough of heart failure)
Ask the patient to cough and listen to its character — barking vs wet vs dry
Inspect sputum sample if produced (purulence, blood)

investigations.why: First-line for any cough beyond 3 weeks, any haemoptysis, or any focal signs — rules in pneumonia (consolidation), TB (upper-zone infiltrates/cavitation), mass lesion, effusion; a normal film shifts weight to asthma, postnasal drip, GERD, or ACE-inhibitor cough

investigations.test: Sputum for acid-fast bacilli (2 samples) / GeneXpert where available
investigations.why: Rules pulmonary TB in or out in any cough > 3 weeks with fever, night sweats, weight loss, or suggestive X-ray — the decisive test in the Iraqi setting
Neutrophilia supports bacterial pneumonia; eosinophilia supports asthma or parasitic bronchitis; normochromic anaemia accompanies TB and malignancy
High values support pneumonia or TB over asthma, GERD, postnasal drip, and drug-induced cough; ESR markedly raised in TB and malignancy

investigations.test: Peak expiratory flow diary or spirometry with reversibility
investigations.why: Diurnal variability or bronchodilator reversibility rules in asthma (including cough-variant asthma with a normal exam); fixed obstruction in a smoker supports COPD

investigations.test: Trial of ACE-inhibitor withdrawal (documented, with physician)
investigations.why: Diagnostic manoeuvre, not a lab: resolution of a dry cough within 1–4 weeks of stopping the drug rules in ACE-inhibitor cough and spares further testing
Second-line — if haemoptysis with a normal X-ray, a suspicious mass or nodule, or a smoker > 40 with persistent unexplained cough; characterises malignancy and bronchiectasis the plain film cannot
